Subject: Atlas Bio — discovery recap & next steps

Hi Sam / Kate — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned.

Key takeaways from discovery:
- Primary objective: pilot to validate real-time inference for sequence analysis pipelines (batch throughput target ~1k reqs/day, ~250 tokens per invocation).
- Data posture: non-PII research data; Atlas prefers EU residency for results but can accept US for an initial pilot if isolated.
- Success metrics: end-to-end latency < 200ms p50 for single-request path, cost per inference target <$0.01 token-equivalent for the pilot workload.
- Constraints: procurement timeline likely late Nov; security questionnaire is next step.

Proposed next steps (from Redwood):
1) Share mutual action plan + one-pager pilot proposal (attached).
2) Technical sync with SE to confirm throughput/latency expectations — target week of Oct 11.
3) Security questionnaire kickoff — we'll send an initial SOC2/data-handling doc.

Could you confirm priority on the pilot and your preferred week for the technical sync? If Oct 11 looks tight we can do a short pre-call before then.

Attachments: discovery-notes-20261003.txt, mutual_action_plan_v0.xlsx, pilot-proposal-onepager.pdf

Thanks —

Quick context: discovery on 10/3; attachments + MAP sent. Prospect intent: pilot evaluation but procurement timing unclear (likely Nov). We want to:
- confirm priority and timeline
- lock technical sync date or get an explicit no-go

Neha — on the technical side I'd keep the bump lightweight but include three quick points we can validate in a 20-min sync:
1) Baseline sequence length distribution (avg vs 95th pct) — we'll size caching and KV strategy accordingly.
2) Tokenization details (they may count tokens differently) — ask for an example payload.
3) Residency requirement: if they insist on EU for results we can run a regional variant but need to confirm storage pattern.

If they share sample payloads ahead of the call we can give a more concrete latency/cost estimate. Happy to join the sync.

— Marissa

Neha / team — agree with Marissa. From CS perspective:
- Offer: 2-week sandbox with a small usage credit (no SLA) — useful to remove procurement friction. We can absorb minimal infra cost for the pilot.
- On onboarding: ask whether they have non-prod data ready; if not, we can provide synthetic payload templates to validate pipelines.

Jordan: if we can offer a small trial credit (e.g., $2k) it usually nudges procurement to respond. If you prefer not to commit without approval I can frame it as "we typically offer a light sandbox credit for proof-of-concepts" and surface exact numbers after their sign-off.
